basis.obligation: Fixed nonblank fixture label goes through real BasisId admission. unwrap deliberately fails the test if this valid fixture is refused.

matrix.signature: fn matrix(rows: usize, cols: usize, entries: &[i64]) -> BasicMatrix<Q>
matrix.obligation: Only small declared row/column/data fixtures are supplied. Convert i64 exactly to Q and use checked row-major constructor; unwrap is the positive-fixture expectation, not a public error handler.

arithmetic_binds_basis_degree_and_vector.body: { let a = Chain::new(Degree(1), basis("a"), vec![q(1)]).unwrap(); let b = Chain::new(Degree(1), basis("b"), vec![q(1)]).unwrap(); let c = Chain::new(Degree(2), basis("a"), vec![q(1)]).unwrap(); let dual = Cochain::new(Degree(1), basis("a"), vec![q(1)]).unwrap(); assert!(matches!( a.add(&b), Err(HomologicalError::BasisMismatch { .. }) )); assert!(matches!( a.sub(&b), Err(HomologicalError::BasisMismatch { .. }) )); assert!(a.add(&c).is_err()); assert_ne!(a.hash(), b.hash()); assert_ne!(a.hash(), c.hash()); assert_ne!(a.hash(), dual.hash()); let x = Cochain::new(Degree(1), basis("b"), vec![q(1)]).unwrap(); assert!(dual.add(&x).is_err()); assert!(dual.sub(&x).is_err()); }
arithmetic_binds_basis_degree_and_vector.obligation: Fixed one-coordinate canonical vectors separate basis, degree and static kind. Assert incompatible add/sub refusals and unequal fingerprints for these concrete inputs only, not universal hash injectivity or global label identity.

map_admission_and_application_reject_wro.body: { use boundary::BoundaryMap; use coboundary::CoboundaryMap; assert!(BoundaryMap::new(Degree(0), Degree(1), matrix(1, 1, &[1])).is_err()); assert!(CoboundaryMap::new(Degree(0), Degree(0), matrix(1, 1, &[1])).is_err()); assert!(CoboundaryMap::new(Degree(i32::MAX), Degree(0), matrix(1, 1, &[1])).is_err()); assert!(BoundaryMap::new(Degree(i32::MIN), Degree(0), matrix(1, 1, &[1])).is_err()); let down = BoundaryMap::new(Degree(1), Degree(0), matrix(1, 1, &[1])).unwrap(); let up = CoboundaryMap::new(Degree(0), Degree(1), matrix(1, 1, &[1])).unwrap(); let chain = Chain::new(Degree(0), basis("x"), vec![q(1)]).unwrap(); let cochain = Cochain::new(Degree(1), basis("x"), vec![q(1)]).unwrap(); assert!(down.apply(&chain).is_err()); assert!(up.apply(&cochain).is_err()); }
map_admission_and_application_reject_wro.obligation: Finite bounded-degree overflow, non-overflow wrong shift for both map kinds, and wrong input-degree cases. The new coboundary 0->0 case isolates target mismatch from overflow. Real constructors provide positive controls. is_err checks refusal, not every exact error variant/order/payload.

unchecked_rationals_and_impossible_alloc.body: { let undefined = Q::new_raw(1.into(), 0.into()); let unreduced = Q::new_raw(2.into(), 4.into()); for value in [undefined, unreduced] { assert!(Chain::new(Degree(0), basis("x"), vec![value.clone()]).is_err()); let raw = BasicMatrix::from_row_major(1, 1, vec![value.clone()]).unwrap(); assert!(certify_rank(&raw).is_err()); let chain = Chain::new(Degree(0), basis("x"), vec![q(1)]).unwrap(); assert!(chain.scalar_mul(&value).is_err()); } assert!(Chain::zero(Degree(0), basis("x"), usize::MAX).is_err()); let empty = matrix(0, 0, &[]); assert!( chain_complex::ChainComplex::new(usize::MAX, 2, 0, empty.clone(), empty.clone()).is_err() ); assert!(CochainComplex::new(usize::MAX, 2, 0, empty.clone(), empty, provenance()).is_err()); }
unchecked_rationals_and_impossible_alloc.obligation: Deliberate raw 1/0 and 2/4 test input never enters arithmetic in the fixture; Chain, rank producer and scalar admission must refuse. usize::MAX zero allocation and malformed complex shapes must return errors. This does not claim arbitrary memory-exhaustion totality.

serde_cannot_bypass_identifier_provenanc.body: { assert!(serde_json::from_str::<ids::ChainId>("0").is_err()); assert!(serde_json::from_str::<BasisId>("\" \"").is_err()); assert!(serde_json::from_str::<TheoremProvenance>("\"\"").is_err()); for wire in [ r#"{"vertices":[]}"#, r#"{"vertices":[1,1]}"#, r#"{"vertices":[2,1]}"#, ] { assert!(serde_json::from_str::<Simplex>(wire).is_err()); } assert!(serde_json::from_str::<OrientedSimplex>( r#"{"simplex":{"vertices":[0,1]},"orientation":0}"# ) .is_err()); }
serde_cannot_bypass_identifier_provenanc.obligation: Concrete zero/blank ID/provenance, empty/duplicate/descending simplex and orientation-zero JSON must refuse. Serde remains real provider; these bounded cases are not exhaustive wire-grammar proofs.

serialized_carrier_is_revalidated_and_ha.body: { let carrier = Carrier::new( 1, 1, 1, ExactMatrix(matrix(1, 1, &[0])), ExactMatrix(matrix(1, 1, &[0])), vec![q(1)], ) .unwrap(); let wire = serde_json::to_value(&carrier).unwrap(); let roundtrip: Carrier = serde_json::from_value(wire.clone()).unwrap(); assert_eq!(carrier, roundtrip); let mut forged = wire.clone(); forged["c1_dim"] = 2.into(); assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Carrier>(forged).is_err()); let mut forged = wire.clone(); forged["weights"] = serde_json::to_value(vec![q(0)]).unwrap(); assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Carrier>(forged).is_err()); let mut forged = wire; forged["d0_hash"] = serde_json::to_value(Hash256([0; 32])).unwrap(); assert!(serde_json::from_value::<Carrier>(forged).is_err()); }
serialized_carrier_is_revalidated_and_ha.obligation: Real admitted zero-matrix carrier roundtrip is positive control. Wrong dimension, zero weight and concrete wrong d0 fingerprint must refuse. Does not cover every field substitution, second-hash fault, serializer type name or valid weight change; separate facade campaign covers broader wire behavior.

graph_constructor_rejects_each_invalid_i.body: { use exact_carrier::graph_carrier; assert!(graph_carrier(1, &[(0, 0)], &[], vec![q(1)]).is_err()); assert!(graph_carrier(2, &[(2, 1)], &[], vec![q(1)]).is_err()); assert!(graph_carrier(2, &[(0, 2)], &[], vec![q(1)]).is_err()); assert!(graph_carrier(2, &[(0, 1), (0, 1)], &[], vec![q(1); 2]).is_err()); assert!(graph_carrier(3, &[], &[(0, 1, 2)], vec![]).is_err()); assert!(graph_carrier(3, &[], &[(0, 1, 3)], vec![]).is_err()); assert!(graph_carrier(3, &[], &[(0, 0, 1)], vec![]).is_err()); assert!(graph_carrier(2, &[(0, 1)], &[], vec![]).is_err()); assert!(graph_carrier(2, &[(0, 1)], &[], vec![q(-1)]).is_err()); }
graph_constructor_rejects_each_invalid_i.obligation: Concrete self-loop, source/target range, duplicate edge, missing triangle edge, repeated/out-of-range triangle vertex, wrong weight length and nonpositive weight cases. Only is_err is claimed, not exact precedence or full payload sensitivity.

rank_certificates_reject_independently_f.body: { let m = matrix(2, 3, &[1, 2, 3, 2, 4, 6]); let receipt = certify_rank(&m).unwrap(); assert_eq!(receipt.rank(), 1); receipt.verify_against(&m).unwrap(); let candidate = receipt.candidate().clone(); // All split identities still hold for this candidate; only M=UV can reject // binding a nonzero factorization to the zero matrix. assert!(RankCertificate::try_admit(&matrix(2, 3, &[0; 6]), candidate.clone()).is_err()); let mut bad = candidate.clone(); bad.image.set(0, 0, q(0)).unwrap(); assert!(RankCertificate::try_admit(&m, bad).is_err()); let mut bad = candidate.clone(); bad.image_retraction = BasicMatrix::zero(1, 2).unwrap(); assert!(RankCertificate::try_admit(&m, bad).is_err()); let mut bad = candidate.clone(); bad.coordinate_section = BasicMatrix::zero(3, 1).unwrap(); assert!(RankCertificate::try_admit(&m, bad).is_err()); let mut bad = candidate; bad.coordinates = BasicMatrix::zero(2, 3).unwrap(); assert!(RankCertificate::try_admit(&m, bad).is_err()); assert!(receipt.verify_against(&matrix(2, 3, &[0; 6])).is_err()); }
rank_certificates_reject_independently_f.obligation: Known rank-one 2-by-3 matrix. Binding nonzero factorization to zero isolates M=UV with the same valid split identities; zero retraction and zero section isolate LU/VR. Corrupt image and malformed coordinates also refuse; the latter may be shape refusal, not an isolated identity challenge. Positive certificate replay precedes faults.

rank_inequality_does_not_replace_the_cob.body: { // rank(d0)+rank(d1)=2=dim(C1), yet d1*d0=[1], so the law fails. let d0 = matrix(2, 1, &[1, 0]); let d1 = matrix(1, 2, &[1, 0]); assert!(matches!( carrier::Carrier::new(1, 2, 1, d0, d1, vec![q(1); 2], provenance()), Err(HomologicalError::CoboundaryLawViolation { .. }) )); }
rank_inequality_does_not_replace_the_cob.obligation: Explicit d0=(1,0)^T,d1=(1,0) have ranks 1+1=C1=2 but product [1]. Require the law-error variant; rank-only admission is decisively rejected.

exact_rank_fixture_exceeds_fixed_width_a.body: { let big = num_bigint::BigInt::from(1) << 200usize; let m = BasicMatrix::from_row_major(2, 2, vec![Q::from_integer(big), qr(1, 3), q(0), qr(2, 7)]) .unwrap(); assert_eq!(certify_rank(&m).unwrap().rank(), 2); for (r, c) in [(0, 0), (0, 3), (3, 0), (2, 3)] { assert_eq!( certify_rank(&BasicMatrix::zero(r, c).unwrap()) .unwrap() .rank(), 0 ); } }
exact_rank_fixture_exceeds_fixed_width_a.obligation: Exact BigInt 2^200, 1/3 and 2/7 upper-triangular matrix has nonzero diagonal and rank two. Empty/zero rectangular shapes have rank zero. No fixed-width narrowing or binary floats.

all_two_by_two_ternary_matrix_ranks_matc.body: { for code in 0..81usize { let a = (code % 3) as i64 - 1; let b = ((code / 3) % 3) as i64 - 1; let c = ((code / 9) % 3) as i64 - 1; let d = ((code / 27) % 3) as i64 - 1; let expected = if a * d - b * c != 0 { 2 } else { usize::from([a, b, c, d] != [0; 4]) }; assert_eq!( certify_rank(&matrix(2, 2, &[a, b, c, d])).unwrap().rank(), expected ); } }
all_two_by_two_ternary_matrix_ranks_matc.obligation: Base-three code bijects 0..81 onto all four entries in {-1,0,1}. Products/difference fit i64 (absolute determinant<=2). Nonzero determinant gives rank two; otherwise nonzero entry gives rank one, all-zero rank zero. Independent Fraction row reduction audits every case.

graph_betti_numbers_match_combinatorial_.body: { // Every labelled simple graph on four vertices; H1=E-V+components. let possible = [(0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 3), (1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3)]; for bits in 0..64 { let edges: Vec<_> = possible .iter() .enumerate() .filter(|(i, _)| bits & (1 << i) != 0) .map(|(_, e)| *e) .collect(); let components = four_vertex_components(&edges); let c = exact_carrier::graph_carrier(4, &edges, &[], vec![q(1); edges.len()]).unwrap(); assert_eq!(c.dim_h1(), edges.len() + components - 4); assert!(carrier_manifest::CarrierManifest::from_carrier(&c).verifies(c.as_ref())); } }
graph_betti_numbers_match_combinatorial_.obligation: Enumerate all 64 subsets of six fixed ascending four-vertex pairs. Only this bounded family feeds helper. Each edge merges at most one component, so E+components>=4; E+components<=10, preventing subtraction/addition overflow on this fixed domain. Compare E+components-4 to exact core H1 for unfilled graph, plus actual manifest replay. Fraction incidence rank and transitive closure independently audit all expected cases. No triangle or arbitrary graph coverage claim.

four_vertex_components.body: { let mut labels = [0, 1, 2, 3]; for &(a, b) in edges { let from = labels[b]; let to = labels[a]; for label in &mut labels { if *label == from { *label = to; } } } labels .into_iter() .collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>() .len() }
four_vertex_components.obligation: Exact extracted label loop. Caller only supplies fixed endpoints 0..3, so indexing into four labels is safe. Before each edge, equal labels represent connected components of the processed prefix. Replacing every old component label by the other merges exactly the endpoint components; loops/idempotent merges preserve partition. Distinct label count is component count. No extra allocation inside merge; final bounded BTreeSet matches previous code.

simplicial_limits_roundtrip_and_known_to.body: { assert!(SimplicialComplex::standard_n_simplex(usize::MAX).is_err()); assert!( SimplicialComplex::from_simplices(vec![Simplex::new(vec![usize::MAX]).unwrap()]).is_err() ); let disk = SimplicialComplex::standard_n_simplex(2).unwrap(); assert!(disk.coboundary_matrix(usize::MAX).is_err()); assert_eq!(disk.rational_betti_numbers().unwrap(), vec![1, 0, 0]); let wire = serde_json::to_string(&disk).unwrap(); assert_eq!( serde_json::from_str::<SimplicialComplex>(&wire).unwrap(), disk ); // Boundary of the tetrahedron is S2: independently known Betti vector. let facets = [vec![0, 1, 2], vec![0, 1, 3], vec![0, 2, 3], vec![1, 2, 3]]; let sphere = SimplicialComplex::from_simplices( facets .into_iter() .map(|v| Simplex::new(v).unwrap()) .collect(), ) .unwrap(); assert_eq!(sphere.rational_betti_numbers().unwrap(), vec![1, 0, 1]); assert_eq!(sphere.euler_characteristic(), 2); }
simplicial_limits_roundtrip_and_known_to.obligation: Extreme simplex/coboundary inputs refuse. Disk has contractible Betti vector [1,0,0]; boundary of tetrahedron is S2 with [1,0,1], Euler 2. Exact finite simplex/boundary/quotient models support these interpretations. Roundtrip checks admitted disk only; no direct Simplex.face orientation sensitivity or arbitrary topology classification claimed.

formal_specification.failures: Assertion/unwrap failures intentionally fail the harness. Negative raw/huge inputs are passed to declared provider boundaries; no silently caught panic or disabled test.

failure_paths.test_failure: Every assertion/unwrap intentionally propagates to the Rust harness, whose nonzero result is retained. No catch-all, cfg(any()), ignored case or test-source mutation.
failure_paths.fixture_safety: Fixed endpoints fit four labels; exact i64 ternary determinant fits [-2,2]. All unbounded inputs are deliberate refusal probes. BigInt 2^200 and nonzero rational denominators retain exactness.

trust_boundary.formal: Pinned clean Lean/Mathlib proofs of the referenced exact matrix/rank/scalar/coordinate/incidence/quotient properties. Finite independent Fraction/transitive-closure audit establishes bounded expected oracle values, not Rust extraction.
trust_boundary.runtime: Captured Rust harness/std, actual unchanged local providers and pinned dependencies. Standard assert/unwrap failure semantics and checked matrix/BigRational providers. Source/model/fixture correspondence is explicit review.
trust_boundary.scope: Local root homology only, not the separately resolved omega_homology Cargo package or full application.

consumer_review: Enclosing root mod.rs activates this file with cfg(test). Runner selects all twelve tests directly under the same native module context, including controls before/after. Ten providers are actual imports of these tests.
The helper is called only by the fixed four-vertex graph family. No external public API, authority-bearing artifact or user contract added.
assurance_limits: A is scoped source/model/finite native evidence, not A+, Rust/MIR extraction, allocator/crash totality, hash injectivity or exhaustive production-provider coverage.
Faults are injected into production providers, with assessed consumer code unchanged; mutation accounting names this scope explicitly. Historical provider-own challenges remain separate.
Original test-body nesting-four B ceiling is retained with its exact source/view. The extracted helper reduces current maximum nesting without removing cases/assertions. Contracts remain pending.

G1: Every test/helper body, fixed input domain, actual provider and expected result has an explicit source-pinned obligation. Checked mathematical models retain their literal statements; finite oracle audit pins independent calculations, not authority promotion.
G2: Exact rational/BigInt fixtures only; deliberate invalid raw pairs test rejection. Ternary determinant arithmetic and graph indexing/subtraction bounds are explicitly reviewed and every finite oracle case independently checked. Known topology fixtures map to the exact simplicial/quotient models, not a claimed arbitrary-topology proof.
G3: Intentional assertion/unwrap test failures propagate to the native harness. All fixture-positive inputs are bounded/admitted; malformed and resource inputs enter tested production boundaries. No silent catches, disabled tests, unfinished axioms or unvalidated test index.
G4: All 21 designated valid provider faults detected by the final consumer unchanged within each copy, none survived/invalid/equivalent/inconclusive/unrun. All 99 original tests pass before/after, with twelve-test controls for each provider. Initial 20/21 retained: existing coboundary overflow input failed before target mismatch, so skipping target guard survived. New non-overflow 0->0 refusal assertion detects it. Independent exact Fraction rank and transitive closure audit 81 matrices and 64 graphs; source review binds expected values and real failure classes.
G5: Same 64 cases, same four-label partition updates and bounded set count. Extract nested label loop and add one non-overflow mismatch assertion; thirteen other bodies unchanged. No production algorithm or input domain changed. All sixteen bodies measured through the explicit test view; helpers alone do not establish the test-body ceiling.

All 12 test attributes select real harness tests. Opaque assert/assert_eq/assert_ne expand to expected harness failure branches; their arguments contain the recorded provider calls, matches patterns and finite literals, with no hidden loops/recursive methods. matches is bounded pattern matching; vec is finite literal/repeat construction. Source metric does not count assertion expansion as production control flow. unwrap expects positive fixtures and intentionally fails on an invalid implementation, not a public panic handler.
